checks: New native group inherits original HttpOnly cookie and localStorage in the same Chrome profile
Two groups keep different server logins and localStorage after reload; ordinary Chrome remains Original
Two native tabs in one Chrome group share Cookie and localStorage updates
Idempotent localStorage writes do not emit feedback storage events or block sibling-tab requests
document.cookie and localStorage.clear affect only the managed group, including navigation
Native blank tab adopted by a managed group; moving it to another group reloads with that group identity
Closing and reopening a group restores its own login and storage without re-copying the source

Each group contains its own Header rows with individual checkboxes and add/delete controls; edits autosave and apply to all group requests including website-opened main documents; disabling one row preserves its value and other rows, B and ordinary tabs are unchanged
Header feature is optional and disabling restores original request headers; Cookie overrides and CRLF injection are rejected before saving
Website login popup joins its opener group before first request; redirects and response cookies share only that group, with ordinary and B-group identities unchanged
Async blank-popup location assignment and target=_blank links create native tabs in the same session group
GET forms and programmatic POST login forms preserve method and UTF-8 fields, follow redirects inside the opener group, and leave B and ordinary accounts unchanged
Synchronous XHR response cookies do not deadlock the group network queue or pollute the ordinary profile
Enabled per-group Header rules persist across full Chrome restart together with the group login
Full Chrome restart restores the saved group identity from extension storage
Explicitly stopping a managed tab redirects it to an explanation and blocks its HTTP network access
